utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Mr. Registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in the court. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Laurie Sartorio, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to our learned friends from the Prosecutor's Office, to everybody in the courtroom and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson representing General Delic, and Lejla Gluhic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I notice the witness is not in court. Is there any issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There is an issue concerning protective measures for an upcoming witness that my understanding was perhaps should be raised at this point in time. We would be prepared to address this issue either at the current moment, later -- sometime later today at the completion of this witness's testimony, or perhaps tomorrow, at the Trial Chamber's choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Take your pick. When do you want to do it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would actually prefer to do it perhaps tomorrow afternoon, early. It does concern a witness who's scheduled to appear later this week. However, I'm not finished proofing this witness, and I might have additional information once I'm finished meeting with the witness. But I am entirely in the Trial Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have the dominant status, so we are in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would prefer doing it, Your Honour, at the completion of the current witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If he could then be brought into the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May the witness be brought into court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Please sit down. Good afternoon once again. Let me just take this opportunity to remind you, sir, that you are still bound by the declaration you made --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'll start again. I'll start again. May I just remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't realise that your mic was not on, there was no translation. That is what I was going to say, but now that has been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. You may recall that at the close of yesterday's session, we looked at a document, marked Exhibit Number 599, and it was a monthly coordination plan for July of 1995. Do you recall that last document we looked at?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Then I would like to move directly into our next document. May the witness please be shown P02378. And while waiting for the English first page to come up: Sir, can you identify what this document is?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a coordination plan of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia -- of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina for the month of August. It is identical to the previous plan that we looked at, but this one is for August.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And again did you participate in the preparation of this plan?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And if you take a look at the plan just briefly, it's page 25 of the English and it is page 13 of the Bosnian version, and particularly I want to draw your attention to where it talks about tasks of the 3rd Corps Command. And then you may have to move over to the next page so both the Judges and the witness can see the whole section - right- of this section, and I'm just going to ask a brief question. I need to see more on the English. We need to go down on the B/C/S version, please. Thank you. And I think the Judges have probably read that first sentence. If we could go over to the next page in English, please. The question I'm going to ask, sir, is: This plan doesn't -- doesn't to me seem very specific, so what is the purpose? Is this a general plan, and then if so, what stems from this, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us clarify. The coordination plan concerns the life and work of units and installations, their life and work. This should not be confused with the coordination and concerted action plan, because these are two different concepts. This is a coordination plan which concerns the life and work of every individual unit and installation or institution in the military, meaning that units had the obligation to submit, once a month to the General Staff at the Kakanj command post, their activities which they intended to implement in the following month. All the administrations were likewise under the obligation to submit a list of their activities, and the Operations and Planning Administration, in cooperation with the other administrations, had the task of consolidating all these, of putting them together, to coordinate them and that is why it is called a coordination plan, a coordination plan, and it is very important to understand which concerned the life and work of units, as I've already explained, whereas concerted action, that type of coordination is quite a different thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, may the document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next exhibit number will be number 00600.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now may the witness now be shown P02324, please. Oh, see if it's been admitted. That's Exhibit 532, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to identify this document for the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a monthly analysis of combat readiness of the 3rd Corps for July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So would this report -- would each corps have to come up with a combat readiness -- each corps that would be involved in a particular operation would have to prepare a combat readiness report?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly, but in this particular instance it is obvious from this document that the task was and that this is a monthly analysis. Every month, the Corps had to prepare an analysis of the combat readiness, but I cannot recall whether one was sent every month by them, and where this monthly analysis was sent to, because you cannot see it from the document. I'm not sure whether the Corps made it for its own purposes or sent it to someone, dispatched it elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. We may put away this document, since it's been admitted in evidence already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now may the witness please be shown P02359.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, now, if you see this document, is this a document that is coming from the 328th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says, the 328th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And to whom is this document addressed?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is addressed to the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the date of the document, would you agree, it's the 3rd of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the document -- at least the English version, and hopefully the Bosnian version, says "Regular Monthly Combat Report"; is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is written here "Monthly Regular Combat Report."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So this represents one report that would be sent from a brigade to a division; right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And if I may direct the witness's attention, it's page 12 of the English version and it's page -- there's no page. It's number 6, enumeration 6 in the Bosnian. There's no page numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to tell us what is being addressed in this particular paragraph with relation to the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which paragraph, Madam Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In the English version on the screen, it's at the bottom of the page, so we may have to move up. Okay. And in the Bosnian version, it appears -- I'm not sure that's the same paragraph. I'm not able to read Bosnian, but I see "El Mujahedin" there, so I thought it would -- is that the same? Can someone -- yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is not the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm looking for that paragraph in the Bosnian version. Well, rather than waste time, I'll move on, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, that is page 5 of the Bosnian version, the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't appear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Isn't that the sentence --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It doesn't appear to be the same sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The penultimate bulletin on the --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The penultimate bulletin, the penultimate bulletin, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, "bullet."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What are you looking for in English, what are you looking for?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm looking for the same paragraph that starts with: "The number of informal talks between the PK for moral guidance and officers of the El Mudjahedin Detachment."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then that should be the penultimate bullet on the Bosnian --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, penultimate bullet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you see that section, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us what this is addressing?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, as far as I remember, we talked about this document yesterday, and this concerns a report of the Brigade sent to the Division. I said yesterday that I did not wish to talk about that document because the same had not been sent to the Kakanj command post, so that it had never reached me. But if you wish me to analyse this and if I have to, I will certainly do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, were you aware that there were some issues concerning the El Mudjahedin Detachment and malfunctioning and problems that arose between some soldiers of the army, other soldiers of the army, and members of the El Mudjahedin Detachment? Can you address the subject matter?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not privy to that. That is why I said that I didn't want to talk about this document, because I was not familiar with the situation. I don't know what it was about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. The document may be put away, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is put away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness be shown document P03027.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to identify this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- these are conclusions and tasks for a meeting of the Corps of the General Staff of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina with corps commanders. It is conclusions and tasks emanating from a meeting of the Corps of the General Staff of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina with corps commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And if you look on the second page of this document in both versions, please -- okay, well, it must be -- the B/C/S is the first page. I'm sorry. Where it talks about conclusions and tasks. So where did this meeting take place, according to this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just take a look. It is not stated here, but it was probably held in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And who would have been present at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here the core staff, the core section of the General Staff of the Army, and that implies the commander, the chiefs of Staff, the heads of Administrations, unless one was absent, and the corps commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We just noticed, Your Honour, that the translation is not accurate on this document. The dates are different, and the reference numbers are different. Oh, no, actually, no, that's -- it says the "2nd of August."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know how often these types of meetings occurred in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very often, because this was at so high a level, they were not held very frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you be more specific, what "not very frequently" means?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps twice a year, but I can't be sure of that. I'm not positive. I just suppose that it was two or three times a year.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we ask that this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document shall be given Exhibit number 00601. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What is the relevance of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The relevance of the document, Your Honour, is to show regular and detailed reporting on the part of the units and the Corps and meetings being held, especially at this critical time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It should not come as a surprise to the Chamber that meetings were held and reporting was made, so unless you have any particular point that you wish to raise in the document, I suggest you consider the risk of entering too many documents into evidence, because it burdens the trial record and afterwards, when we sit back and look at all these documents, it's just going to tie us down. So please be careful and --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- make sure we understand the reason why you put these things forward to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I will take that into very serious consideration, and I think I'm moving on now from general reports to some more specific reports that do address the issues before the Court. Thank you. May the witness be shown P02213.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, if you look on the right-hand side of the first page, it appears -- did this document come to your command post in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a regular daily combat report submitted by the 3rd Corps Command to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the Kakanj command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you identify what the subject matter -- given the title of the document, what it's about?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the very title says this is a regular daily combat report. I think that is sufficiently clear, the way I put it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you agree with me that the date of the document is the 6th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now I'd like to direct the Chamber's and the witness's attention to it's page 2 in the Bosnian and page 3 in English, please. Under section 2, sir, where it discusses situation and activities of the 3rd Corps forces, 35th Division, do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us what, if anything, that section says with regard to the El Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written here that in the zone of responsibility of the 35th Division, units are still in a full state of combat readiness. The activities of the 35th Division Command are still directed at -- it is not quite clear what it says. It says here "bringing in," probably should be "carrying out," carrying out preparations to continue the Proljece-95 operation. During the day, senior officers from the detachment -- from the El Mudjahedin Detachment spent time with the Division Staff in order to coordinate tasks for the upcoming operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, we ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document shall be given Exhibit Number 00602. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May the witness please be shown document P02221.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, I'm going to ask you, even though I know everyone can read, but for the record can you please identify the date of this document and to -- who was it from and to who is it addressed, or who does it go to? Does it go to the General Staff at the Kakanj command post or not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you already said it, the date is 8 July 1995. It was sent by the 3rd Corps Command to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, at their command post in Kakanj, and this is a regular daily combat report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And just briefly, what is the substance of this report?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a regular daily combat report, and I've repeated it several times today. Regular daily combat reports were sent with the purpose of informing, and I believe it is very clear if something is called "Regular Daily Combat Report," what is the document about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. But my specific question is: I would just like you to state, in a sentence or two, what the substance is of this regular daily report. It seems to be about some preparations between some units, so could you please just state for the record what it is about?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regular combat reports have their elements. For example, here the first is the current situation and the activities of the enemy forces and of the United Nations. The second item would be the current situation of our forces, you know. Further on, the fourth item would be neighbours. The fifth item would be the functioning of communications, the sixth would be the state of morale, the seventh would be logistics, and so on and so forth. These are the elements of the combat readiness that every combat report has to have their elements that a combat report has to have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, sir. The interpreter is struggling desperately to keep pace with you, you know. Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. Now the second -- and just -- I don't want to press this because of time, but the second factor seems to address joint combat operations between the El Mudjahedin Detachment and the 328th Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it here. Could you please assist me and tell me where you see it, and then I will gladly read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's under section number 2, which is on the second page in B/C/S, and it is at the top of the page --

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: "Yes" what?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of responsibility of the 31st [as interpreted] Division, fighters from the 328th Mountain Brigade are carrying out final preparations for the upcoming combat activities, together with the El Mudjahedin Detachment. This was also part of the former report. We spoke about that, and the same thing repeats in this combat report. The thing that we saw in the previous combat report is here repeated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your Honours, may this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It will, ma'am, but again let me just follow up what Judge Harhoff asked a little earlier. I notice that the El Mudjahedin Detachment is mentioned here, but isn't it -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness, as you may recall, was supposed to come at an earlier time where, in the logical sequence of the Prosecution's case, we were discussing command and control over certain aspects of the army, and these documents are relevant for that purpose. I know we seem to have moved on in terms of the trial, the witnesses, but he was supposed to come a few weeks ago on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And we have heard witnesses testify on command and control.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, these are -- I will stick to documents that only are -- that only mention what are -- the heart of the case is, but I think it's important that we have these documents as part of the record to show the joint combat, unless ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio, the point is made. We have understood and we have accepted, and it is, I believe, not disputed by the Defence that these meetings took place. Maybe it is. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I don't want to anticipate what the Defence's position is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But I think we have to be careful not to make the admission of evidence too repetitive.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I think it's contested that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Joint operations?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, that were under the control of the ABiH, and our theory is this document supports our theory of the case that they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The document shall be given Exhibit number 00603. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I have one moment, Your Honour, to speak with my colleague? Thank you. Your Honours, may the witness be shown P02270.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to identify this document, please?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. This is another identical document, very similar to the previous two. The Command of the 3rd Corps sends its regular combat report to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the BiH army at the command post in Kakanj. The form is the same. I've already described the form. The contents may differ a little.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for Your Honours, the whole document has not been translated into English, but the part that I want to draw the Court's attention to is. It's on the first page, and so when we ask to submit it in evidence, we will have to supplement when the translation is prepared. I would like to direct the witness's attention to the first main paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That's the activities of the enemy, if we're talking about the first paragraph that I can see on the screen right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour. It's on page 2 of the B/C/S, please, where it says -- talking about the 35th Division. It's probably 12 lines down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this is referring to, this particular sentence here?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that the forces of the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion were regrouped from the area of responsibility of the 1st Corps to the area of responsibility of the 35th Division. The furlough of the units has been approved around 2200 hours, and also the forces, on the strength of the 329th Mountain Brigade and the 5th Manoeuvre Battalion, they have also been regrouped in the village of Cardak in order to link up with the El Mujahid Detachment forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, we ask that this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we admit the document in evidence, I see the transcript says something was approved at 2200 hours. The letter -- the document says at 20 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, I think we have to go with the B/C/S version and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Does the B/C/S version come up with 2200 hours?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It says --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, Witness, can you tell us the time of that what you just read, the time that is indicated in your document? Is it 22 hours or 20 hours, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's 20 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I believe that's a typo in translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says 2000 hours on the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct, and I thought the interpretation had earlier said "22 hours."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It did, Your Honour. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I heard in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, the translation that came across to us in court just now -- or a few minutes ago was "2200 hours." What did you -- what is your answer? Is it 22 or 20?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "20" here. I probably said "20." I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And did you ask that the document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This document is given Exhibit number 00604. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness now be shown document P02360.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, could you tell us the date of the document, what it is, and who it's from, and who it is going to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another identical document, again a regular combat report similar to the previous three that we have analysed also. The 3rd Corps Command sent it to the General Staff in Kakanj. Again, this is a regular daily combat report just like the previous three.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But they are all different dates; is that correct? The different dates of the reports we've been looking at --

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one was sent on the 3rd of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I'd like to go to page 2 in the English, and it's also page 2 in the B/C/S version. It's the section under "35th Division." Sir, can you tell us what this says with regard to the El Mudjahedin Detachment, what this report is relaying?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that: "During the day, the El Mudjahedin Detachment troops were withdrawn from the area of defence of the 328th Mountain Brigade in order to rest and prepare for offensive combat activities, providing that 60 fighters have remained at the P/K," which probably stands for "the forward line of defence."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, we ask that this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, I'd like to move on now, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The document is given Exhibit number 00605. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to move on from regular daily combat reports and ask you whether other types of reports that were submitted by the units or by the Corps, and the Corps particularly to the forward command post in Kakanj? Were there other types of reports, and if so, do you have a name for those reports?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understood your question properly. Would you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, why don't I show you a document, and we can talk about the document. May the witness please be shown P02261. Now, sir, would you agree the date of this document is the 18th of July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is stated herein.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the document was addressed to the forward command post in Kakanj; correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "the General Staff of the BiH Army," the Kakanj command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And this is -- is this a daily combat report or is this an additional, or interim, or some other type of report?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All it says here is "Report." That's how they would call it, a report. It doesn't say that it was a daily, regular, interim report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. But if you look at the first line of this document, it -- at least in the English, it says: "In accordance with your orders ...," okay, so what -- can you tell us what this -- is this a regular daily combat report or is this some type of, what it appears to be, a response to an order?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a reaction to an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio, I guess --

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kindly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I guess we would have to see the order in order to be able to ascertain the correct answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, under number 1 of this document, can you please read what that says?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kindly show me the order number 1/825/1276 and the other order dated 17 July, if at all possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, it isn't at this time, and what I'm asking you to do is just tell -- tell the Chamber what is contained in this paragraph of this document that was addressed to the forward command post at which you were located.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, you were located in Kakanj, at the Operative and Planning Administration; correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but not at the forward command post, as you put it to me before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Fine, sir, but these documents, the reports that would come in, they would come in to the -- would they come in to the Operative and Planning Department?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not arrive at the Administration for Organisation and Planning. They arrived at the Communications Centre, which forwarded them to the duty operations officer's post, the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the duty operations officer post, was that located in the Operative and Planning Department, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The duty officers' rota was composed of all the officers that were there, and those officers could come from any department or administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we ask that this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Hold on. Mr. Alija, what is the significance of the line in paragraph 1 that says that: "The time of the readiness for action will be determined by the K-da Command of the detachment, since the El Mujahedin is the primary leader of the upcoming task"? Who is the "K-da"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my document, it says the time of the readiness for combat will be determined by the detachment command, given the fact that the El Mujahedin is the unit in charge of the upcoming task. Since you've asked me, I would like to answer your question. That means that the El Mudjahedin Detachment will determine -- and I would kindly ask you to listen to me really carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Rest assured, we are listening to you very carefully.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, please? Here it is confirmed, and this is a very important thing and I'm very glad that you've noticed this thing, the time will be determined by the El Mudjahid Detachment, which means that they will do what they have to do whenever they want to do it, which is a confirmation of the fact that this was a very specific unit which, in my knowledge and according to my information, was not within the system of control and command. They were a closed unit, and they stood for themselves. They were independent. They were very difficult to reach or receive information about their activities. They made their own decisions. Most probably, Your Honours, I believe that you know that they had their own way of decision-making. That term is "shura," is something like a council of sorts. And if they decided to do something, they did it. And if they decided not to do, they didn't do it, and they would not take anybody's orders. That's why there's a sentence here, just one sentence, that is very few words for something that could have been put in many more words, and the essence of the matter is that they will do things the way they want to do them. This is what I wanted to tell you. I would kindly ask you, since I've already discussed this document, I would kindly ask you to give me the other document that is referred to herein, because I was probably the author of that other document and I would very much like to see it. The number is 1825-1276.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's best that we leave the examination-in-chief to the Prosecution. But my question to you was really: What does it mean, that the time of readiness for action will be determined by, I now understand, the Command of the El Mudjahid Detachment, because apparently that detachment is the primary leader of the upcoming task. That was my question, because it could be understood to mean that the leading force in this upcoming task, whatever that is, has been left in the hands of the El Mujahid Detachment. Is that a correct reading of the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partly, not wholly. This is for this particular task, but we cannot apply that across the board, but we cannot do it before we see other documents. That's why I would kindly ask you to give me this other document. We cannot go into any further discussions without it. More specifically, this is just one task. The El Mujahid is not a leading task or the leading force in the 35th Division. The leading force was the Army of -- the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you can't draw conclusions. You need to stick to facts. You are not in a position whereby you can interpret text or establish links between various documents. This is our role, not yours. Leave it to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I was asked a question, and I'm duty-bound to answer the question. The Judge asked me something, and I have to answer, and that's what I'm doing, you know. And I would kindly ask you to allow me to answer the question that the Judge has just put to me. And when I do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, but you haven't only answered the question the Judge asked you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did answer. I said that it was not the leading force. The Judge asked me whether they were the leading force. I said that they were not, which means I've answered the question. And I'm fully prepared to answer your further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will appreciate you answering our questions, but also not to start giving us a whole history, which we are not asking for. You said quite a lot when you were first asked about this point which I thought went far beyond giving an explanation of that sentence. But the sentence is quite clear enough. We can see for ourselves what it says. I think the important thing was for you just to explain what "K-da" meant, and that's it. But anyway, that's fine, thank you so much. Judge, are you done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, not quite, because I still fail to understand fully the meaning of the sentence here in this report, which says that the El Mujahedin is the primary leader of the upcoming task, and this fact is adduced to explain why the time of readiness is also left with the Command of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Your explanation was that this might well be the case for this particular task, that the El Mujahid Detachment had been given the leadership of that upcoming task, but you were also, in your testimony, apparently keen to underline that this was something exceptional, this was not an overall or frequent situation, and that is my question to you, then. Do you know if the El Mujahid Detachment, in this particular task, was appointed the primary leader, and do you know if that occurred frequently in other tasks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In respect of this particular task, it is stated here that the El Mudjahedin Detachment is the principal protagonist, the spearhead of this particular mission, and therefore it was the one who would decide the time of readiness for starting the mission. And as far as I know, to the extent of my military knowledge and my experience and the places that I've been to and seen, I believe that the El Mujahid Detachment was not assigned tasks of this kind very often. I should like to ask you again kindly to let me give you a complete answer to this question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Just a second, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're not letting me testify. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I've been asked to say if this was so in this case, the El Mudjahedin Detachment, was it asked oftentimes to lead tasks like this? Just to say, "yes, it was," or, "no, it wasn't." You don't have to give a long story.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But by your leave, I should like to explain more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think we should put it back to the Prosecution. Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, on my exhibit list was this particular order. I wasn't going to introduce it because it's already been marked as an exhibit, but I will for the sake of -- for completion. It's Exhibit 496, and it was on my list to the Defence as P02244. Yes. May the document be shown to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, can we just give an exhibit number to the previous document. Document 2261 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Exhibit number is 00606. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Now may the witness be shown Exhibit 496. Now, the document in Bosnian is one page, but the Judges may -- can we go to the second page, to the bottom. Second page, please. We can see who initialled.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, did you draft this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I wrote this document. That is why I asked for it to be shown here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And those are your initials, "AI"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are, "AI," that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now if we could go back to the front page of the document, and as I've said, this document has already been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But would you like to comment on this particular document in relation to the last document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would certainly like to comment on it. This is a document that was created in connection with a newly-arisen situation in Zepa and Srebrenica; namely, when at that particular time period in Zepa and Srebrenica, thousands of people were killed, slaughtered, burned out. A genocide, namely, had been committed against my people. The Dutch Battalion, which was there and which was in charge of protecting those people, failed to do so. The United Nations, whose task it was to do that, also failed to do it. So we, in the General Staff, undertook measures and issued orders that at the entire front, at the entire theatre of war, there should be combat operations carried out in order to facilitate the situation for the people and to save the people, because those who -- whose obligation it had been to save the people didn't do it. They let them be killed and slaughtered, thousands of people. It is very hard for me to speak about this document here in Holland, because it was their people who had been in charge of saving the people, but they let the aggressor kill them, liquidate them and slaughter them, burn them out and burn their houses, and commit the more serious genocide after the Second World War in Europe and beyond. That is how this document was created.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to interrupt you, because this is a forum where I ask a question and you provide an answer, and you have indicated your comments on this document. But let me ask you this: What did you mean by "entire front," and what did you mean by "entire theatre of war"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means not only in the Srebrenica and Zepa area, but throughout the battle front where there were units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that in view of the fact that the aggressor's forces in the particular time period had concentrated their forces in the direction of Zepa and Srebrenica and had, therefore, weakened their front which they were holding in other parts of the battlefield, so it was our objective to undertake active operations throughout the battle front in order to have those forces return to their previous positions and alleviate the burden on the part of the battle front which included Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May this document be put away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is put away now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this would be a good time to take a break, and I will decide at that point I will limit my -- the remaining documents, but I need to quickly go through them to pick out the most relevant ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have four more documents. May the witness please be shown P01869. And while we're waiting for the English -- oh, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us if -- can you identify this document for us, where it's coming from?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the Staff of the Supreme Command of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, written at the Kakanj command post, dated the 14th of November, 1994, and it concerns concerted action, coordinated action, in organising, preparing, and there are some letters missing here, you know, so -- in the document that I'm reading. And it is addressed to the Commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And may we go to the second page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is signed by General Enver Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: On behalf of General Delic; is that it? Is that what that --

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does say "for."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the last sentence of this document, can you tell us what that is discussing?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The item 1; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The last sentence about: "The solution should be found to move the El Mujahedin ..."

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some letters missing here in this last sentence, as well as in the penultimate one, so perhaps the sense might be lost in translation. Reading, rather, in reading. Some letters are missing in the text.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Would you recall us looking at this in proofing? Don't you recall looking at this and you gave an interpretation of what it was despite the fact that there were some missing letters?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I did say that there were letters missing, and I asked whether we dared -- whether we had a right to translate it, seeing that letters were missing. If we have that right, please tell me so, but it is quite obvious, as we concluded then as well, that there are letters missing here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. And because of the type -- the diacritics that are on the typing keyboard, but did you tell me that you were still able to make out what this is talking about, because you can fill in the letters?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about it. We came to the conclusion that there were letters missing, and when I asked you whether that had to be translated, you said that it was incomplete on account of the missing letters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to read the paragraph or are you not able to read it without the missing letters? If you're not able to, just say you're not able to and let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that there are letters missing, so I would not want to be wrong there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Move on, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness be shown P01869. Excuse me. That was that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, I'm curious to know what lies behind that last paragraph that you drew the witness's attention to. What was the problem that sparked the determination of the Supreme Command in Kakanj to move the units of the El Mujahid, whoever that might be, out of Zenica as soon as possible and to speed up the construction of the barracks for them? I think you might wish to ask the witness to elaborate a bit on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, that's -- thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, there was -- I think you heard what the Judge said, and there was -- are you aware of the fact that there were some attempts or some movement made to move the El Mujahedin into some barracks and away from where they were at the time? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I ask you to focus on the title of the document, namely, the date, the 14th of November, 1994, when I was the deputy commander of the 4th Corps in Mostar. In other words, I was not at the command post in Kakanj, in the General Staff, so that I don't know anything about this document, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. We're putting the document away, and now I'm just asking you in general: Are you aware of the situation where they had to build barracks to move the El Mujahedin out of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, and I believe that is contained in my previous response. No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May the witness now be shown P02865.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, would you agree that this -- the date of this document is the 22nd of December of 1995, and it's a regular combat report?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it is written here "the 28th of December." It is not the 22nd. It is the 28th of December, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I stand corrected. It looks like an incorrect translation again. And this is a -- did you answer -- confirm whether or not this is a regular combat report that is submitted to the Main Staff of the Army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I'd like you to look at number 3 under the document. I'd like the witness to be shown section 3, and also on the English it's on the second page or -- second page. Sir, this report -- this section under number 3 is discussing -- what is it discussing, sir?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written here: "The combat morale of units in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps," and that morale can be appraised, generally speaking, as good. "The focus of activities of the Department for Moral Guidance and Political Issues is on organising an appropriate send-off ceremony for the members of the El Mujahid Detachment which will be held shortly."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your Honour, I would ask that this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your Honours, we ask that this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 607.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness now be shown P02308.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you identify what this document is?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an interim operative report, and it is sent from the 3rd Corps to the -- it is sent to the General Staff from the 3rd Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The General Staff at the command post Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like the second page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, I'd just like to draw your attention to the paragraph that begins discussing the El Mudjahedin Detachment. And could you explain what that paragraph is describing?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written here that forces of the El Mujahedin department and other units, the 4th Battalion and the 7th Brigade, carried out offensive operations, attacks, during the day, and the El Mudjahedin Detachment, at a specific direction or axis, the village of Cevaljusa and Nikolino Brdo, routed the forces of the Vukovi Detachment. In the combat that was conducted on this axis, the Chetnik forces suffered losses, the 20 Chetniks who remained on our side, that is, as far as the El Mudjahedin Detachment is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your Honours, we ask that this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 608.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And finally may the witness please be shown P02315.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, this document appears -- this document is dated a day after the previous report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "the 24th of July, 1995" here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And it's an interim -- another interim combat report?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And it's going to the Supreme Command Staff at Command Post Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And if you look a little below halfway down, do you see where it refers again to the El Mujahedin and the 328th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is this a continuation of the reporting from the operation that was taking place?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not confirm that with certainty, but it says here that the forces of the El Mujahid Detachment and the 328th Mountain Brigade forces, which, by the way, are not referred to in the previous report, successfully removed the forward line of defence in the Nikolino Brdo and Ravne areas on the stretch "S," meaning village of Cevaljusa, Nikolino Brdo, Ravne, Podsjelovo. There is reference to the 328th Brigade here, and there was no such reference in the previous one so I'm not sure whether it is indeed a continuation of the previous mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's fair, thank you. Your Honours, we ask that this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 609.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We have no further questions. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'm Vasvija Vidovic and I will be leading you cross-examination on behalf of Rasim Delic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The nature of any cross-examination is such that to a majority of my questions you will be able to answer either by "yes" or "no," and since I have quite a lot of questions for you and my time is limited, I would kindly ask you, whenever possible, please provide very short, simple answers. A mere "yes" or "no" will do unless I ask for some additional information, either I or the Honourable Chamber. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Alija, you graduated from the military academy in Belgrade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have a lot of experience working in various posts in the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the BiH Army, you also discharged various high duties and you held various high offices; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were the chief of the Command of the 1st Corps, in the 1st Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you were the chief of Staff, thank you. After that, as you've already told us, you worked in the Staff of the Supreme Command, at the command post in Kakanj, and I will go back to that in some detail later on. And now I would like to ask you briefly about the rules and regulations of the former JNA, since you used those rules and regulations before the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, isn't it, that these rules and regulations were actually -- served as a base for the BiH Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, at the beginning of the war, for a very brief period of time, applied the regulations of the former JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, because we did not have our own regulations at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, already in the summer of 1992, passed its own regulations, decrees and bylaws which regulated the control and command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A decree on defence was passed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that, a decree on armed forces?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later on, I will go back to the experience that you amassed as the chief of Staff in the Corps, but now I would like to show you the documents that the Prosecutor showed you yesterday. Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 597. Do you remember having seen a schematic yesterday? While the document is being shown, can you remember having seen a schematic yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you document PT1389. This was an order by the SVK, and do you remember that the schematic was an integral part of that document; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask you to look at the same schematic again. In your testimony, you said that you didn't know whether this was a schematic that was in effect in the course of 1995; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also told us that the schematic was rather unclear. You mentioned some ambiguities about the name, the acronyms "SVK" and the General Staff; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document please be put away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this schematic, you added certain things?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the schematic was incomplete. It said here "the 8th Corps," and I don't think that the 8th Corps ever existed or was a part of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, can the witness now please be shown P01839. This is a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that not already an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, the Prosecutor tendered the schematic, but not the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at the document. Will you agree with me that you've already seen the document dated 18 October 1994?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The title was "Reorganisation of the BiH Army"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The organisation order. And now can you go to the second page of this document, both in English and in B/C/S. I am looking at bullet point number 7. Yes, we can see it. Please look at bullet point number 7.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, will you agree with me that it says here that the Department for Organisation and Mobilisation of the Superior Command Staff will draft new establishment of the General Staff, of the Corps Command and the Division Commands in accordance with the schematics 1, 2, 3 and 4? 4 --

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- which are enclosed with the document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you then agree with me that this item 7 says that the schematic is pending, that it is yet to be drafted?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read this here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please be shown page number 7 in the Bosnian version, which is the last page in the English version. In other words, it is the last page in both the B/C/S and the English versions of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at bullet point -- let us please see the English page that was on the screen previously, that we just had on the screen, because we would like to look at bullet point number 29, which is probably page number 15. One page before this one, if you could. Can you find the signature page, which is a few pages before this one? Yes, just a moment. I believe it will be the previous page in the English version. Yes. Could you please display bullet point 29, which I believe is on the previous page of the English version. The previous page of the English version. Yes, that's it. Now we can see it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, I hope you've been able to read the paragraph in your own language while we were waiting for the same page to appear in the English version. Will you agree with me that these parts, i.e., this part of the document, shows that the chief of Staff and chiefs of administrations and departments will prepare a proposal for the organisation of their respective departments and that all the positions and opinions will be coordinated, and it is here suggested that this should be done in the way as per schematics 1 to 5; can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that these parts of the document, this one and the bullet point 7, clearly indicate that these schematics were nothing but the working material based on which the final instruction on the internal organisation of the General Staff of the Army should be drafted?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask for this document to be given an exhibit number; the entire document, that is, including the schematics. And, Your Honour, in the meantime I am going to show the witness the schematic that I believe is really important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 610.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit number 419.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see that this is a document issued by the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina which had passed a decision, i.e., a schematic on the organisation of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it very clearly. This is a decision of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the schematic of the future organisation of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at the last page of the same document, i.e., page 4 in the Bosnian version and page 6 in the English version. Can we please see the signature block.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this document was passed on the 24th of October, 1994, that it was signed by the president of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we saw a document issued on the 18th of October, 1994, which was just a proposal, and will you now agree with me that this now is a decision of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, let me ask you whether you will agree with me that the Presidency was in charge of passing a decision on the schematic of the organisation of the army?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was within their purview.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, could you please look at the other provisions, where it says, on the day when this decision is passed, the decision on the schematic of the organisation of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, number so-and-so, dated 14 December, 1993, is now made null and void; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And am I right in saying that no other schematic of the organisation of the BiH Army was no longer in effect as of the 24th October 1994 but this one that was passed on that day; am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we go back to page 1 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You explained to us that the Presidency is the supreme command of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I'm not going to ask you that, but please look at page 2 now, item 3, which is page 2 in the Bosnian version as well as in the English version, reappointments. Do you agree, Mr. Alija -- renaming, actually. As we are talking about the 20th of October, 1994, it was on that day that the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was renamed "the General Staff of the Army"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is why I said, when discussing the diagram, that it was not quite clear, and this actually specifies what refers to what very precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please be so kind as to look at -- actually, I would like to quote, first of all -- I apologise. What I want you to do at this point is to look at this subtitle "Organisation of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina," and please go through it. Will you please read it for yourself?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have, I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you agree with me that the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina comprises the -- consists of the General Staff, the Air Force and Anti-aircraft Defence Commands, six corps, the East Bosnia Operations Division, three independent brigades which are actually designated here, the Guards Brigade, the 10th Mountain Brigade and the 1st Reconnaissance Sabotage Brigade, the Black Swans, Crni Labudovi, and that a chart has been made accordingly, which is attachment number 1 to this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, will you please reply to this question: Mr. Alija, it would be erroneous to believe, would it not, that all the units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were under the direct command and control of the Army General Staff, i.e., its commander?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are quite correct. It was impossible for the commander to control all units. There were hundreds of other units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The essence of my question is this: It is true, is it not, that specific units were designated here in this paragraph? You can look at item 2 again. So the units are precisely spelled out, and who is directly subordinated to the commander of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. If we can now look at item 5, Your Honours. Can you scroll the down document a bit. In the Bosnian version, it is on this page, and in the English version, on the following page. Witness, please take a look at item 5 of this document. It says the following here: "The following shall be directly subordinated and linked to the Army General Staff commander, the Air Force and Anti-aircraft Defence commander, and the commanders of the units referred to under item IV/I of this decision." Also the Deputy commander and the chief of the Army Staff, and it goes on to list the rest of the subordinates. So is it true that -- when I say -- am I right when I say that the corps commanders are directly subordinated to the General Staff commander, and the rest who are specifically listed in this item; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right. The commanders of the corps and of these administrations that are listed here in this item.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and of the administrations listed here in this item. And now please look at page 7 of the Bosnian version, page 7 of the Bosnian version, which is page 11 of the English version, Your Honours. Can we take a look at chapter number 5 or passage number 5, looking from the top, or the third from the bottom, if you like. In the English, that is the second passage from the top of the page, which begins with: "The present number of corps ..." Witness, I shall quote this part of the explanation, which says: "The present number of corps shall not change. Instead of operations groups, which were formed as temporary units, making it impossible to appoint officers to duties within operations groups, divisions are established within corps. Besides divisions, one mobile manoeuvring brigade is formed in each corps under the direct commander of the corps commander who thus exerts his influence on the main axis of combat activities." My question is: Do you agree that this document says -- this part of the document, namely, specifically explains that under the direct command of the corps commander are divisions and mobile or manoeuvring brigade with which the corps commander exerts his influence on the main axis of combat activities?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that. That is what it says here, and that is how it has been in force, and it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the way that this functioned in practice?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I shall kindly ask you to let me finish my question. So is this the way this functioned throughout 1995?
