utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the way it functioned, the corps, divisions, brigades, battalions and companies and platoons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, divisions were directly subordinated to the corps commanders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Alija, this decision that we have seen actually determined that the commander of the Main Staff directly commanded corps commanders, issued orders to them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, excepting certainly here those units who were directly commanded by the General Staff? I'm talking about the principle here. And it is also correct, is it not, that the corps commanders could be directly commanded also by the deputy commander of the Staff of the Supreme Command, when he was standing in for the commander, or according -- or under his authority, the authority of the former; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Working in the JNA, as a former JNA officer, and in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you certainly must know what the principle of the unity of command is in military doctrine.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, unity of command and subordination.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The principle of unity, singleness of command, was adopted in the regulations which concern control and command in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That means that the commander could not -- cannot interfere in the authority of the first subordinate commander, the first subordinate commander to him, in the sense of issuing a direct order to the unit which is under the command and control of his subordinate or an even lower-ranking subordinate; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. This is the basic principle of the unity of command, where the commander issues commands and orders to his first subordinate, and then that subordinate issues further orders to his subordinates, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The same also is true of reporting, is it not? This is what you told us, actually, in responding to the Prosecution's questions and explained.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A lower-ranking unit, for instance, a battalion or a detachment, cannot directly report to the Corps Command, for instance?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it definitely cannot. It must first report to its superior command, which is the brigade, the brigade to the division, division to the corps, and the corps to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I believe that this is already an exhibit and can be now moved away, please. And can the witness at this point be shown document D402, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A while ago, you mentioned the General Staff administrations. Do you remember that? And you can see that this is a document of the Supreme Command Staff of the Operative Centre of Command from Kakanj. The date it bears is the 1st of January, 1994. In connection with this, I should like to ask you this: So, as you worked in Kakanj, the principle was -- the principle work was this: You told us that every administration had its head, there were administrations, so am I right to assume that every administration had its own head or chief?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As regards these administrations, they also communicated, did they not, both in terms of ordering and reporting, with organs of a lower level, that is to say, with lower-ranking organs; for instance, the Administration for Moral Guidance of the General Staff with the Corps section for Moral Guidance; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right when you say that, because everybody communicated on the basis of their line of specialty, the logistics organs with the logistics organs in the Corps, the Administration for Moral Guidance with the Department for Morale Guidance in the Corps, the Administration for Security with the Department for Security in the Corps, the Intelligence Administration with the intelligence organs in the Corps, so they communicated along specialist/professional lines and exchanged information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This process was a two-way one, if I can say so. Yes, we shall slow down a bit, Mr. Alija. So if I can say that -- if I can say so, as far as the orders coming from the top to bottom, from the administration towards the sections, the departments, going down towards the first subordinate level and then the second one, this is the way the process went; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the reporting process was exactly the opposite; from the first lowest level to the higher -- next-higher level and on to the General Staff; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, may this document please be admitted and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 611.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us, Witness, that a significant period of time is spent working as the chief of Staff of the 1st Corps of the BiH Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was the chief of Staff for a brief period of time. I spent much longer as the deputy commander of the Corps, but, yes, I was the chief of Staff of the 1st Corps as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about certain duties that the chief of staff of any corps has to discharge. Am I right in saying and in thinking that a chief of staff has to discharge its duties pursuant to the instructions and decisions of the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some of the decisions -- some of the duties are discharged independently?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I was going to say next.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The chief of Staff is in charge of the work of the Staff through the professional organs in the Staff. He monitors the operative and tactical positions of the corps in the field; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are absolutely right. Those are just some of the duties that a chief of staff discharges, in addition to everyday duties and activities, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He also analyses combat and other capabilities of the corps; am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He also looks at the situation in the field?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He also analyses combat reports received from the subordinated units?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He drafts combat and other documents which are of significance for combat activities work and life in his unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course assisted by the organs that he has on the strength of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, that's true. He is also somebody who coordinates the planning of operations and actions executed by the corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He also maintains communications with the chiefs of staffs of the subordinated commands; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He also informs the commander of the situation and problems that have been noticed in the corps?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, he's the one who proposes to the commander as to how to solve and deal with certain problems; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now, on behalf of the corps, the commanders of the corps communicate with the Supreme Command Staff along the command lines?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the professional lines, it is the professional organs that communicate with each other? And I'm here referring to administrations and departments.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For example, the Security Service of the 3rd Corps will communicate with the Security Service of the Supreme Command Staff, if that is -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to ask you something about the position and role of the command post of the Supreme Command in Kakanj and also the other one in Zenica. You will agree with me, won't you, that the situation, in terms of the command of the BiH Army, that the war situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina for the BiH Army was very specific, it was not a typical situation? And I will explain why I'm putting it in this way, and you can answer me then. The capital, Sarajevo, was under siege of the Serb forces, and that's where the Command was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Likewise, the areas that were under the control of the BH Army were intersected by the enemy formations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was why a majority of the Supreme Command Staff, in 1994, left Sarajevo in order to improve their situation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina is where the commander of the Staff and his office remained, together with a smaller number of various administrations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was necessary because he, by his position, was also a member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and he was duty-bound to attend the sessions of the Presidency; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was a very important reason, but also the commander often participated in the talks that were held in the capital, at the airport, so that he had daily activities in the capital.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you now referring to the context with the representatives of the international organisations?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The international organisations, and I also refer to the talks that were organised at the airport with UNPROFOR -- actually, the talks that were organised by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I see. I believe you're talking about the peace talks --

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- that were very intensive in the course of 1994?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were very frequent meetings at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This means that these negotiations were held very often in the course of 1994 and 1995; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Can the witness please be shown D403.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I hope that you will manage to read parts of this document. Let me just say for the record this is an article from the daily "Oslobodjenje." The date is the 23rd of July, 1995. I believe that you can tell me something about the facts that are referred to in this article. Your Honours, I don't think that the witness can see anything. Maybe we can blow up the version in the Bosnian, the language for the witness, the part that is under the image. If not, then we can provide the witness with a hard copy of the same page. In this case, the Trial Chamber does not have the English version, so maybe we can provide the witness with a hard copy of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But maybe it would be best if you could have it in the hard copy as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, this article refers to the agreement between the state delegations of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia in Split, and the title of the article is "Joint Defence Against the Aggressor." I believe that you know and that you're aware of something that was well known in the army as "the Split agreement."

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now kindly ask you to look at the part that is immediately under the title. It says here that the two state delegations, after the talks, signed a declaration on the implementation of the Washington Agreement, the joint defence against the Serb aggressor, and achieving a political solution. And you can see that it says here that this was done in Split on the 22nd of July, 1995. Can you see "Split, 22nd July 1995"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you look at the fourth paragraph. And for the Trial Chamber, this is the second paragraph in the English version, in which there is a list of the members of the delegation. Will you agree with me that it says here "Brigadier Ramiz Delic"? Please, do you know that General Delic was representing the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina at these negotiations in Split?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Supreme Command Staff, you knew about the peace talks?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 612.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would like to correct the translation, because the name in the translation is spelled wrongly. I have to check, but it seems to me that the name is spelled wrongly. It says "Ramiz Delic" instead of "Rasim Delic," so we would like to correct the written translation of this document where the name is misspelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You mean the English translation of the exhibit said "Ramiz Delic" but I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- I didn't look at the B/C/S, but it did say "Ramiz Delic." We can look at it again. Can we bring that exhibit again, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, yes, we can do that, but I would like to clarify one thing with the witness in the meantime. My version is now in the hands of the witness, so I can't see whether there was another Delic save for the General Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not in the General Staff. There was a Sead Delic in the 2nd Corps. That was another Delic in the BiH Army. As for the General Staff, there was only Rasim Delic, the commander of the General Staff. There was no Ramiz Delic. No Ramiz Delic existed in the General Staff, as far as I know. There was no General Ramiz Delic, to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that General Rasim Delic participated in the peace talks in Split, in the so-called "Split Negotiations"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just mention that the Delic in this exhibit, on the English version, is actually a brigadier, it's not a general.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I noticed that myself. That is what I'm talking about, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The name of Mr. Delic is not mentioned here. Is the witness saying he has independent knowledge that he attended? Is that the testimony?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is. Yes, it is, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And is it also possible to have a look at the copy that he has, the B/C/S copy that he has. I guess these names are listed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I believe so, Your Honours. Perhaps if we could just enhance these parts which are in bold print. It is written "Brigadier General Ramiz Delic." The translation is incorrect. They said "Brigadier" instead of "Brigade General Ramiz Delic," which is quite clearly written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where is "Ramiz Delic" here? Is it "Ramiz," not "Rasim"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It says "Ramiz."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is written "Ramiz Delic," but it says "Brigadier General Ramiz Delic," so I think it is a typo. This is a war paper, Your Honours. I shall certainly clarify it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree with me that there could have been no other -- that there did not exist any other brigadier general in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina except for General Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just explained that, and I'm surprised that they wrote "Ramiz Delic" in this paper. It was probably a typographic error.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there did not exist any other brigadier general?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There was a Sead Delic, but in the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I believe, Your Honours, that we can, and I propose that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just ask one question. What was the rank of Mr. Rasim Delic at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He had the rank of general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not brigadier general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not quite sure what rank of general he had, but it was a general's rank. Later, he was promoted, so I'm not sure at that particular point, but it was definitely a general's rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Could we enlarge this exhibit again, please, yes, just to make -- to zoom on it, around the name there. Thank you very much, thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document -- thank you very much. It has been admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Witness, we have come across the issue of "brigadier" and "general" a few times during this trial, and if you know, could you then explain to us if indeed a brigadier is the lowest of the general ranks or whether it is something that it's a title that does not relate to the level of generals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the rank of brigadier is between colonel and general. That is not a general's rank, brigadier, whereas in other European and world armies, that is the first general's rank, whereas in our army it is the rank between the colonels and the general ranks, but not a general rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That was very useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just get clarification on something you said a little earlier, sir. When I asked whether Mr. Delic was a brigadier or general, you said: "I'm not quite sure what rank of general he had, but it was a general's rank. Later, he was promoted, so I'm not sure at that point -- particular point, but it was definitely a general's rank." My question to you is: Later, what was he promoted to?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must have misunderstood me. Senior officers were given ranks all the time. General Delic was a general then, on that date. I don't know exactly how many stars he had. That is why I said what I did. He was an army general, and he had four stars, in other words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Listen to my question. My question relies on the last sentence: "Later, he was promoted ...," and I'm asking you: What was he promoted to later or were you misunderstood by the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said that he was promoted, that meant that he was given another star. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, still being a general. Thank you so much. That explains the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to ask a question. This is not an official document, this is a newspaper's article, so sometimes journalists are not as accurate in their reports when they report ranks or others. So this possibly isn't as important as it may appear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. If at this point the witness can look at Exhibit 281. This is also a very fuzzy copy, but I believe that when we blow this document up, that you will be able to see. And if we can enlarge the first part of the Bosnian version of the document, where the date and the heading can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see what this is about?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Organisation of the deployment of the Staff of the Supreme Command of the Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And the date is the 16th of February, 1994. Mr. Alija, please be so kind as to answer this question: The Staff of the Army is certainly not the same as the Supreme Command Staff; am I right? I'm talking about the Army Staff.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I correct when I say that the Staff of the Army is an operational body of the Staff of the Supreme Command, which is associated directly with activities concerning combat operations?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now kindly take a look at this document below. Can you scroll the document down. Can you see the order? Stop it now. Do you agree that this order regulates, i.e., says that the Staff of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, this operational body, in other words, in order to function better, is to be relocated to Kakanj, and then it goes on to list the segments and the administrations that are to be transferred to Kakanj; do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see that, but I don't see where they are being relocated to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean it is not written that it is going to Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Staff of the Army, in order to function better and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but take a look under "B," to the broader area, to the general area of Kakanj, the village of Biljesevo, Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the area to which they will be redeployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is where you worked?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the Operations Centre for the planning, preparation, organisation, and monitoring and implementation of the combat activities was wholly transferred to Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you worked in the Administration for Operative Planning?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your chief was Mr. Asim Dzambasovic, was he not?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The activity of your department was to draw up global documents and plans of significance for the improvement of the situation in the BH theatre of war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the activity of the administration, and our department was part of the administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the department undertook global analyses of the situation in the BH theatre of war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Operations Centre, there was a team that monitored the situation in the BH theatre of war every day and registered all the breakthroughs and losses of territory?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a duty officer in the Operations Centre on duty at all times, and in each administration there were heads -- there were senior officers who conducted activities related to their own specialty in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. We will take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We will no longer need this document, and I would like to start talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want the document admitted into evidence, Madam Vidovic? Oh, it was an exhibit. Thank you, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Operation planning is something that I wanted to ask you about. Since you worked in the Staff of the Supreme Command, would it be true that the Supreme Command defined the strategic goals of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina? I'm now referring to the Presidency. The Presidency was the body, therefore, that acted as a supreme command and, as such, defined the strategic goals of the Armed Forces of the Republic of the Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like now to show you a document. This document is number D404. This is a document issued by the General Staff. The date is 8 March 1995. It seems that the document was signed by yourself, on behalf of the commander, and for that reason I believe that you know the context that was in place when this document was created. The investigator of the Prosecution showed that document to you when you provided your statement?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the document and tell me whether you will agree with me that the document bears the date 8 March 1995.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that it refers to a meeting of the Military Council, that it is actually an order?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to focus on the lower part of the order, where it says that the briefing should be timely to the president of the Presidency and that it should deal with all the elements of combat readiness. Do you remember the occasion when this document was drafted, you provided a statement to that effect to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was drafted on the 8th of March, as you already said it yourself, and given the newly-risen situation in the theatre of war, the commanders of the corps were invited, as well as the commander of the Air Force and Anti-aircraft Defence, to brief the president of the Presidency on all the elements of combat readiness in order to provide him with a picture of the situation at the front line so as to enable the president of the Presidency, i.e., the president, to take appropriate measures with regard to the situation in the theatre of war, i.e., in Bosnia and Herzegovina as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you a very specific question. Was there a meeting with President Izetbegovic after this date to deal with certain issues?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, did that meeting have anything to do with the Sarajevo operation, i.e., the attempt to lift the blockade of the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, I believe that it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now what I would like to ask you is this: You mentioned yesterday, in answering the Prosecutor's questions, the Sarajevo operation, and you also said that you knew that there were teams in the General Staff that were dedicated to the Sarajevo operation. And in this regard, I would like to ask you this: It is true, isn't it, Witness, that the Sarajevo operation was the only operation in the course of 1995 that had been planned at the level of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. The only planned operation was the Sarajevo operation, and the others --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't mean to interrupt the flow, but I don't recall at all speaking about teams and being in -- dedicated to Sarajevo, whatever that is. Do you have a reference, because I don't even know what it means, "teams," so I wouldn't -- I don't recall asking any questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know how this was recorded. I was not talking about the Prosecutor asking those questions. I said that in answering the Prosecutor's questions, the witness spoke about the Sarajevo operation and that there were certain teams planned at the General Staff level for the Sarajevo operation. I didn't say that the Prosecutor put a question to that effect, but that in answering the Prosecutor's question, the witness mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Give us the reference, Madam. Give a reference, and we can see whether the witness said "teams" and in what context he said so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately I cannot do it right away. If you could just bear with us for a moment, I'll be able to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, we will bear with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He spoke in some detail about the Sarajevo operation, and I can see these parts. He mentioned that he saw -- or used to see General Delic. I'm sure you will remember that. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Give us a reference, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 66, Your Honours, page 66 of yesterday's LiveNote. I can see, in lines 17 and 18, and actually the lines from 17 through 23, a reference was made that -- at this very moment -- Your Honours, it would be easier for me to rephrase the question and put it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, actually, I'm not that interested in the teams, they're not necessary for my question. Witness, you mentioned the Sarajevo operation, and I want to ask you this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I help you?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's page 4113 at line 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I see it now, Your Honour, so I withdraw the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The purpose of my question, Witness, is the following, please: In principle, the Sarajevo operation was the only operation that, in the course of 1995, was planned at the General Staff level; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In principle, combat operations were never planned at the General Staff level; am I correct in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like to say something else. The General Staff, at the beginning of the year, drafted a directive for the entire year, based on which the corps worked throughout that year.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before that, can this document be given an exhibit number, and then I'll go back to my question, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 613.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, I'm not sure I fully understand the relevance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the simplest possible way, of course. What I'm trying to prove is what we included in the pre-trial brief of the Defence, which is that the Sarajevo operation was the only operation which had been planned at the General Staff level, and this document shows that there was a meeting that the witness is aware of, and at that meeting, which I'm going to elaborate later on through some other documents, this is the document from which the planning of this operation started, the Sarajevo operation, that is. This is the initial document in the process of planning of this Sarajevo operation. At least this is the way I understood the whole thing. But the witness is here. Maybe he can help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You have elicited from the witness the evidence that the Sarajevo operation was the only one which the General Staff planned on its own, and that I will accept with no hesitation, but I can see no reference to this fact in this document. So I'm just wondering what is the meaning of it. And secondly, of course, my concern is even if we accept the facts that the Sarajevo operation was the only one which was planned and carried out by the General Staff, then what is the significance of that fact? How does this bear on the case against the accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my client is charged with planning, ordering and commanding combat operations in July and September 1995 in the area of Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I don't want to belabour this point particularly in the presence of a witness, but the Prosecution, in the indictment, has -- and in the pre-trial brief, more specifically, has discussed the issues of planning and ordering, as they go to notice. Obvious, this is a 7(3) only case, and General Delic is not specifically charged under Article 7(1) of the Statute. We have included evidence that go to the issue of ordering and planning as those relate to notice and knowledge that he may have possessed, which we allege he possessed, with regard to the El Mudjahedin Detachment being involved in the operations which have formed part of this case, but I do take issue with my learned colleague's statement as reflected on lines 13 to 15 of page 69, that her client is charged with planning, ordering and commanding combat operations. And perhaps it was an interpretation error, but I do want to set the record straight, that he's not charged with that. We have adduced evidence of that, however, as to the issues of knowledge and notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I could see it coming this way, and that was exactly why I raised the point of the issue of planning the Sarajevo operation. Maybe we should ask the witness to take off his earphones. Mr. Alija, I'm sorry, can you take off your earphones? I understand that the witness does, himself, understand English and that he will understand your answer, anyway, so maybe we should just drop it at this point and move on. But I would like to challenge the Defence on this issue. We can do that when the witness has left the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Vidovic, I would like to ask for clarification to the witness. Witness, to one of the questions put to you by Madam Vidovic, you said the General Command, at the beginning of the year, prepared a directive for the entire year, on the basis of which the corps in fact functioned throughout the year. What exactly did you mean when you said that the corps functioned on that basis throughout the year? What exactly are you referring to? What kind of functioning or what kind of work were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This means the following: At the beginning of every year, the General Staff would prepare a document under the name of "Directive." A directive is a document that encompasses general activities in the theatre of war, which was at the time Bosnia and Herzegovina in this particular case. The directive encompassed all the corps, and such a directive would provide or give a global task to every corps in their respective areas of responsibility; not just one very precise task, but a global overview of several activities that every particular corps had to carry out in the implementation of that directive. After that, the corps had been given a global task that they would implement in the course of that year. That was their duty. And the essence of the matter is that later on, they could independently plan operations that stemmed from the directive. A corps is such a unit that has personnel capabilities that allow it to plan its own operations independently. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, the operations within their zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the time being, could we have this document marked for identification? Or maybe it has already been admitted. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought it was admitted as Exhibit 613.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. And now, Your Honours, I would like to go back to the issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have just explained what each and every corps did. In other words, corps commanders would receive a task to provide the General Staff with their proposals of their main focal tasks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I understood your question fully. What do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's start with the directive. A directive is the most important document drafted by the Staff of the Supreme Command, headed by the chief of Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This commander of the Staff of the Supreme Command approves the directive; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after he has been briefed by the chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And then it becomes the basis for all the corps commanders, for their independent planning of operations, in keeping with the tasks provided by the directive; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And at this moment, Your Honours, can we see Exhibit number 384.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I believe that you can see this directive now, dated the 5th of January, 1995.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know this document, you're familiar with it, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This directive was prepared at the Kakanj command post?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was drafted by different departments. Different departments did their own segments of the directive?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The administrations did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, the administrations. For instance, the Department for Operations assessed the possibilities of its own forces?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the Administration for Operations that did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the Intelligence Administration prepared an assessment of the enemy's forces?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And so on and so forth. Look at page 6 of the directive, which, Your Honours, is page number 2 in the English version. Take a look at this part. It is towards the bottom of the page. Can we see this -- yes. The part which starts with: "I decided ..." Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I have decided that in the coming defensive combat operations, firmly hold the taken line of defence, continue carrying out offensive combat operations of operative and tactical importance with particular focus on the army, with the following objective: freeing the temporarily-occupied territory; lifting the blockade of the encircled free territories in the Drina River valley; lifting the blockade of Sarajevo; join the forces of the 4th and 7th Corps with those of the 6th [as interpreted] Corps; cut off important roads used by the aggressor for supplies and evacuation; take control of important roads and industrial facilities for our own needs; and create conditions for the final liberation of our homeland."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that these were the focal objectives of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and that is what this decision says.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the further course of events or in the further text, there are the specific tasks for the individual corps. Take a look at page 7 of the Bosnian version, which in the English, Your Honours, is page number 3. You don't have to read this out aloud. Just reads the tasks assigned to the 2nd and 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you scroll down a bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please enable the witness to see item 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question, Witness, is this: This directive for 1995 actually ordered the 2nd Corps to liberate Vozuca, and do you agree that this is a very broadly-formulated order, without the specification of any precise tasks?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. This is a directive which issues a global task and joins up of the 2nd and 3rd Corps to liberate the general area of Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that the Corps Commands were absolutely independent in planning the Vozuca operations in September 1995?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true, these are operative units that then planned their own operations independently.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In giving testimony yesterday, you told us that you had hardly heard of the Proljece operation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Supreme Command Staff did not take part in the planning or control and command of combat operations in Vozuca in July 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It did not have any part in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The July action at Vozuca in July 1995 was planned at division level, was it not, if you know that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure. I don't know, in fact, about the activities which were carried out there, but they were not planned at the General Staff level.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The General Staff did not approve this action, either?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seeing that it had not planned it, it could not have approved it either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document can be taken away, and can we look at Exhibit number 386 at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, can I just get confirmation, sir. You say this document is a directive from the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, it's already admitted. Thank you, thank you very much. And you called for 386, Exhibit number 386?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, 386, Your Honours. This is a General Staff of the Army document of the 26th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will recall having been shown this document by the Prosecution's investigator when you made your statement?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The date on this document is the 26th of August, 1995, and its title is -- or rather its subject, "Taking measures pursuant to the directive for 1995, order." Can you scroll the document down so that we can see the rest of the text, please. Judging by the initials that we can see on the document, one would say that you are its author?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the Bosnian version bottom part of the document, please. That is the second page in the English version, Your Honours. Can we see the second page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the place where there should be a signature, there is written: "Commander, Army General Rasim Delic"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the bottom left-hand bottom corner, it is stated "Approved." Do you recognise this signature?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First and foremost, tell us whose signature it is.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Brigadier Dzambasovic's signature, who was my superior at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Asim Dzambasovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you agree that I'm correct in saying that General Delic was not present when this document was produced in Kakanj, he was not in Kakanj at all?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're quite right. Had he been there, he would have signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's exactly what I was going to say. In such a situation, it would not have been Brigadier Dzambasovic to approve the dispatching of this document; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are quite right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that General Delic approved the directive for 1995, and this order focused on the realisation of the directive in the segment which concerned the Vozuca pocket; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall how it was that you actually drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember. As always, I was issued an order by Brigadier Dzambasovic. I wrote it up, and after I wrote it up, I would send it on for further processing, as was customary.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this document orders the 2nd and 3rd Corps Commands that they should carry out preparations and elaborate documents for the liberation of the Vozuca pocket area?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, that was what was the substance of this order, and it was also contained in the directive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, actually Their Honours cannot see what we are discussing, so if the first page of this English version document -- of this document in the English version could be shown on the screen, please. That is it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So item 2 regulates the request for the General Staff in Kakanj to be submitted the corps plans for their approval; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened further in putting the directive into practice was that this order was dispatched to the corps commanders, who defined the tasks of only their subordinates; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the commander of the division would be issued a task from the corps commander to prepare a combat operations plan for the division and then submit the division's plan to the corps commander for his approval; right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this process continued all the way up to the battalion level, or down to battalion level, rather?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and down to company level.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the superior commanding officer approves the plan for the execution of combat operations of a subordinated, the subordinated officer then elaborates his own plans independently; is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The planning of actions for Vozuca, or rather the Vozuca action in September 1995, was done by the corps commands independently; right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say "operations," because "action" is not an appropriate term for the mission that was being under undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This document, being an exhibit, can be taken away now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we take it off, let me just ask a clarification question, sir. This process that you say went down to battalion and company level, did it also not go up beyond the corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The corps issued its orders and dispatched them to the division. The division had to act on those orders and to report to the corps. The division would follow suit vis a vis lower-ranking subordinated units, which would then also report to the division of any measures they undertook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question. Once the corps had approved its plans and it was ready to act, didn't it submit those plans up for approval before operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mainly, the corps is such a unit, it is an operative unit, it is a large unit. It is issued a directive. On the basis of that directive, it has a number of courses of action, a number of tasks, and is able to independently plan its activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please try to listen to my question and just answer "yes" or "no." Did the corps, having drafted and concluded its plans, not send it up the chain of command for approval?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it all depends. Sometimes yes, and sometimes no. If it is associated with a directive, no, but if there was a new plan, then yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But this order, which is written on behalf of the accused, says: "The formulated plan of action is to be sent to the Republic of BiH General Staff, Command Kakanj -- Command Post Kakanj for approval and the settlement of other issues regarding its successful execution." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just draw your attention to the fact that it says "to the realisation of a part of the directive," so this just refers to one part of the directive, and that can be sent, and this document requires it to be sent to the General Staff by the 2nd and 3rd Corps Commands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Obviously, a corps is attending to a part of the general directive. All I'm asking you is that: This paragraph 2, isn't it calling for the corps to send up their plans for approval? You know, don't cloud the answer with a lot of explanations. Just say, "Yes, it does," or, "No, it doesn't," or, "I don't know." Then we know exactly what your answer is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As per item 2, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And generally, when corps plan their combat operations, don't they send them up for approval?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a bit specific, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm asking you general. You have answered me on this one. Forget about this one. Listen to my questions. I'm asking you generally, doesn't that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In principle, yes, in principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, thank you. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can we please go back to something that needs to be clarified. The actions that are planned by the corps, in principle, have to be submitted for approval by General Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If an activity has been planned by a division, in that situation such a plan does not have to be submitted to General Staff for approval?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It would have to be submitted to the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Very well. And now I would like you to deal with the issue of combat reports that arrived from the subordinated units to the command post in Kakanj, and I would like to ask you this: The combat reports arrived in the Operations Centre from the subordinated units to the Staff of the Supreme Command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not arrive from divisions or brigades if those were not subordinated to that body. Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally were privy only to the reports that arrived in the Operations Centre; that's what you explained to us, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was accessible to the duty operations officer -- officer in the Operations Centre. That person would make an overview of all the reports and brief the chief of Staff or Brigadier Dzambasovic about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Can we please look at document D046, please. D406, please. Thank you, 406.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the Bosnian version?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the Staff of the Supreme Command in Kakanj. The date is the 31st of January, 1994, and it concerns with the timely submission of reports. Can we scroll down a little to show the whole document, please. Would you agree with me that -- and this is probably on page 2 of the second version, or maybe it has not been translated. Can we go to the second page of the English version for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, please. Can you please confirm that this document was submitted to all the corps?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the very beginning of this document. Will you agree with me that the Staff of the Supreme Command insists on the significance of the truthful and timely reports and information for the system of control and command?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go back to page 1 in the English version, please. The English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now, Witness, can you please pay attention to item number 4. Can you see it? It's: "Fight for complete truthfulness of reports and information. Take the severest measures in case of their false representation." I should like to ask you this about the document that is in front of you: It is true, isn't it, that the Supreme Command Staff, when it came to reports, did encounter the problem of incorrect and false reports that were blown out of proportion?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes; hence the reason for this document to ask for truthful reporting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this document reflects the position of the Staff of the Supreme Command with regard to the importance of truthful reporting?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 614.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We no longer need this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that the way of reporting was regulated by an order? Will you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The reporting from Kakanj to Sarajevo, to the president of the Presidency, i.e., the commander, Commander Delic, was also regulated by an order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now at this moment, Your Honours, can the witness please be shown Exhibit 371. This exhibit consists of two documents. Both are orders of the Staff of the Supreme Command at the Kakanj command post, dated 27 December. Please look at this order. It says, under 1, Corps Command: "Combat reports from the corps which are sent should be sent to Kakanj." Since you worked there, can you tell us whether this order functioned, whether this procedure functioned in practice?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know how this can be possible. The interpretation of my question on page 84 does not reflect what I asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What line?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lines 8, 9 and 10. I asked the witness, reporting from Kakanj to Sarajevo, to the president of the Presidency or Commander Delic, was also -- I apologise, it is correct. I apologise, it is correct. I apologise, Your Honours. This is a correct translation. Your Honour, instead of "i.e.," it should read "or," and then the meaning it is completely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is completely -- it becomes completely different.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was the mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then what is the answer of the witness to the completely different meaning now? Let's get that on the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness was listening to my questioning in the Bosnian language, but I can repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the question is as follows, actually: Reporting from Kakanj to Sarajevo, to the president or General Delic, was also regulated by an order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And for clarity's sake, "the president" refers to the president of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can the witness please be shown the following page of this document. This is another document dated 27 December.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that this document refers to the order that refers to sending reports to all administrations? Can you see that, and do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very legible, I must say. It is barely visible. Now it's better. Now it's better.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you can see it. So you will agree with me -- maybe I can give you that page. Here it says summary combat reports will be submitted by the administrations, and you testified about that yesterday. It is true, is it not, that only short, summary reports were sent from Kakanj to Sarajevo; brief overviews, that is?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only the most important things were derived from the corps reports. A summary was drafted and sent to these addresses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this moment I would like to say that I no longer need this document, and at this moment I would like to show you another exhibit. The number is 598. I believe that you've already seen this document. It was shown to you earlier by the Prosecutor. Actually, it was yesterday that you were shown this document. This is a document issued by the Command of the 3rd Corps, dated 29 June 1995. This is a regular daily combat report submitted to the General Staff at the command post in Kakanj. Let me just remind you and show you the second page, a part that was already shown to you by the Prosecutor, but please bear in mind the date, 29th of June. Can we now please show the witness the second page in both the English and the B/C/S versions. Actually, it is page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please pay attention to the part where spring is mentioned and where a reference is being made to the El Mudjahedin Detachment in the first long paragraph. Do you remember that you looked at the document yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will no longer need this document. I would like to show the witness document D575. Please just retain the information -- retain the information "El Mudjahedin Detachment" and "29 June 1995". And now can you look at D575.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you read this okay? This is a summary combat report dated 30 June 1995. The title is "Situation in the BiH Theatre of War for 29 June 1995". Can you see that? With regard to this, I would like to ask you the following: Reports were always sent on the following day for the previous day, when it came to the situation on the front line; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now you can see the activities of the aggressor, you can see the activities of our own forces, and now kindly look at the part where -- can the document be scrolled down a little, the Bosnian and the English version, please. No, the English version is okay. The Bosnian version, please. Can you please look at the part that concerns the 3rd Corps, i.e., the part where the activities of the 3rd Corps are described, amongst others.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And here, when it comes to the activities of the 2nd, 3rd and the 4th as well as the 7th Corps, you will agree with me it says that -- actually, this reference is very brief, and what I can see here and what I would like to ask you is this: Do you see anywhere the information about the El Mudjahedin Detachment that the Prosecutor showed you in the previous document?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't see it in this document at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this is just an example of a summary report that you used to send from Kakanj to Sarajevo, to the president of the Presidency, and the commander of the army, and some other addressees?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is just an example of that. The others are very similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to show you the second part of the document, if I may, both in English and in B/C/S. Witness, please, will you agree with me that -- can we see the end of the document, scroll down the document so we can see the document in its entirety. Do you agree with me that here there is a handwritten remark: "Processed by cryptographic protection on 30th June 1995 at 0920"?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it obvious, then, that the document was sent to the addressees, protected by cryptographic protection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be admitted, and this is the place -- oh, no, I'm sorry, I still have another 15 minutes to go. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't want it admitted because you have 15 minutes, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I thought that this was the time for me to stop, but I would certainly like this document to be admitted regardless of the time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 615.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit number 602.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at the document. Let's see if we have got the right document. I asked for E602.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it should be a different document. Here we have something different under that number. Your Honours, in any case, I was going to ask questions about this document as well, so I'll go back to it. This is probably my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you did see this document already; you remember?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was a document issued by the 3rd Corps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Now that this is not Exhibit 602, what is this document? You must know what this document is. 602 is dated the 6th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 602, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this 602, this document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I switched two numbers. I made a mistake between 602 and 603. My mistake. I'm the cause of confusion. But this is 602, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I'm still confused, ma'am. What confuses me is that according to my records, Exhibit 602 was a document dated the 6th of July, not the 8th of July, and this document is dated the 8th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you're right. That was my understanding, precisely. That's why I wanted to see the document dated 6th of July. This is the document that I asked for, a document dated the 6th of July. According to our record, this is exactly as you're saying, it should be 602, and this is not that document. Could we be assisted? I believe that this is 603, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It may be, yes. 603 is dated the 8th of July. So you want 602?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we have 602 on the screen, please? It is a document dated the 6th of July?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 6th of July. I believe it is this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you see, having seen this document, too, that is a document of the Command of the 3rd Corps of the 6th of July, 1995, sent to the Main Staff of the Armed Forces at the Kakanj command post, and it is entitled "Regular Daily Combat Report." Do you remember -- and can we show the witness the part on the second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, ma'am. This document is not only sent to the Main Staff of the Armed Forces at Kakanj, but it is also sent to the Main Staff of the Armed Forces, and to Kakanj, and to 2nd and 7th Corps. It's sent to three institutions. There are three bullets.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, it is sent to the General Staff of the Armed Forces at the Kakanj command post, to the forward command post of the 3rd Corps, and to the Command of the 7th Corps; is that right? Now please take a look at this section on the second page which was shown to you by the Prosecutor. Can the witness take a look at item 2, the situation and activities of the forces of the 3rd Corps. Take a look at the part referring to the 35th Division. You can see a reference to Proljece-95 and the El Mujahedin in it?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please just remember this date, the 6th of July. We have discussed it a lot. And this part referring to the Mujahedin. The document can now be moved away. Can we now see document D576. Can you re-enlarge the Bosnian version a bit, or rather show the title to the witness. Witness, if you're able to read this --

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am able. It is a bit difficult, but I will manage.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you cannot, we can give you a hard copy, if you are unable to read it.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you have one at hand, that would be nice, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the English version back on the screen so that the Bench and the colleagues from the Prosecution can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a summary combat report from the 7th of July, 1995, entitled "Situation in the Bosnia and Herzegovina Theatre of War" for the 6th of July, 1995, and the information is being submitted to the president of the Presidency, to the commander of the army, to the Gloc Command in Visoko, and to the Administration for Moral Guidance for Morale in Sarajevo. I'm going to ask you a specific question which refers to the "Activity of Our Forces."

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have the second page in front of you. That is right. Take a look, please. Does it make any reference to the information which you just saw a while ago, which had to do with Proljece and the El Mujahedin? Can we scroll the English version up a bit.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no reference to those here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Rather than scrolling the English version, we can't see anything beyond -- no, no, scroll down, and the next page, if there is any. This is funny. The document in B/C/S is so much longer, and there's just this little paragraph in English. It is only that paragraph that -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will try to explain. I regularly submit to the Translation Service the documents. I regret the fact that sometimes we have documents which are very useful in their entirety, but we are compelled to just have a part of them translated. Anyway, as regards the activities of the 3rd Corps, we had that translated, and that could be of the essence for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you have looked through the document in its entirety. Are the El Mujahedin mentioned anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be given an exhibit number, Your Honours. And take a look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 616.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that this document, too, was also delivered to Sarajevo under cryptographic protection?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the condition that the recipients were in Kakanj, sitting in Kakanj at that moment, would this document have been submitted to them in Sarajevo under cryptographic protection?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If they were in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, then they would have been given -- sent the document to Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Meaning that the document would not have been sent to Sarajevo, cryptographically protected?

utterances.speaker: ISMET ALIJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it means.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I believe that now is a convenient time for us to adjourn, because the next document would require perhaps a bit more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're grateful to you for the couple of minutes you're giving us. Court adjourned, and we'll start tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, the same court. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of October, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.48 p.m.,
